records.context: **A cell is a set of objects.** :func:`cell_rows` is the whole primitive: the rows of the out-of-fold prediction table whose true class is *this* and whose predicted class is *that*. Everything else here is a way of ordering, splitting or counting that set.

records.source: **A cell is a set of objects.** :func:`cell_rows` is the whole primitive: the rows of the out-of-fold prediction table whose true class is *this* and whose predicted class is *that*. Everything else here is a way of ordering, splitting or counting that set.
records.translation: **Uma célula é um conjunto de objetos.** :func:`cell_rows` é toda a primitiva: as linhas da tabela de previsões fora do fold cuja classe verdadeira é *esta* e cuja classe prevista é *aquela*. Todo o resto aqui é uma forma de ordenar, dividir ou contar esse conjunto.

records.context: **A confident error and an unsure error have different causes.** They are therefore two lists, never one sorted list with a gradient in it:
records.label: spacr.confusion#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A confident error and an unsure error have different causes.** They are therefore two lists, never one sorted list with a gradient in it:
records.translation: **Um erro confiante e um erro inseguro têm causas diferentes.** Por isso são duas listas, nunca uma única lista ordenada com um gradiente dentro:

records.context: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the extracted image regions to re-label.
records.label: spacr.confusion#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the crops to re-label.
records.translation: **alta confiança, e errado** — o modelo tinha certeza. Quando um modelo que acerta 95% das vezes está *certo* sobre um objeto e discorda da anotação, a explicação mais provável é que a anotação esteja errada. Estes são os recortes a rotular de novo.

records.context: Handing back one list sorted by confidence buries that distinction in the middle of a scroll. :func:`split_by_confidence` returns the two lists and guarantees they partition the cell, so nothing is silently dropped between them.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.context: Compare measurements across annotated gene groups and remaining cells.
records.label: spacr.gene_measurement_compare#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Compare measurements across annotated gene groups and remaining cells.
records.translation: Compara medições entre grupos de genes anotados e as células restantes.

records.context: Comparisons can use cells, microplate sample positions, or laboratory microplates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a microplate sample position; use the microplate sample position level when microplate sample positions are the experimental units.
records.label: spacr.gene_measurement_compare#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Comparisons can use cells, wells, or plates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a well; use the well level when wells are the experimental units.
records.translation: As comparações podem usar células, poços ou placas como observações. A seleção do teste estatístico é delegada a :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, e cada resultado registra a sua evidência de normalidade, de igualdade de variâncias e de tamanho amostral. Os testes no nível de célula tratam as células individuais como observações e não levam em conta as células que compartilham um poço; use o nível de poço quando os poços forem as unidades experimentais.

records.translation: Uma lista fixa de convenções de nomes de arquivo -- ``cellvoyager``, ``cq1``, ``custom`` (uma expressão regular escrita pelo usuário), ``auto`` -- cobre poucas estruturas reais: das dez estruturas de aquisição em ``tests/import_corpus.py``, duas são analisadas com ela e oito não recuperam nada. records.context: All ten layouts encode the same six facts -- laboratory microplate, microplate sample position, microscope field of view, channel, z, t -- and differ only in how. So rather than matching a whole filename against one of N templates, this module reads the parts of the name that vary across the folder and infers what each varying part means.
records.label: spacr.image_import#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: All ten layouts encode the same six facts -- plate, well, field, channel, z, t -- and differ only in how. So rather than matching a whole filename against one of N templates, this module reads the parts of the name that vary across the folder and infers what each varying part means.
records.translation: As dez estruturas codificam os mesmos seis fatos -- placa, poço, campo, canal, z, t -- e diferem apenas na forma. Por isso, em vez de comparar um nome de arquivo inteiro com um de N modelos, este módulo lê as partes do nome que variam ao longo da pasta e infere o que cada parte variável significa.

records.context: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.label: spacr.image_import#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.translation: A variação ao longo da pasta identifica os eixos. Um token que é o mesmo em todos os arquivos não traz informação: ``L01`` em ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` é uma constante para a placa inteira e não identifica nada. Um token que assume dois valores em oito arquivos é um eixo com duas posições. Só a pasta, e não um único nome de arquivo, mostra quais tokens são eixos.

records.context: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.label: spacr.image_import#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.translation: Os marcadores identificam qual eixo é um token variável. ``F001`` e ``C01`` variam ambos e não são intercambiáveis; a letra na frente nomeia o eixo, e todas as convenções do corpus usam uma. A tabela de marcadores abaixo é esse vocabulário, e é curta porque as convenções compartilham, em sua maioria, as suas letras.

records.context: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.label: spacr.image_import#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.translation: Nenhum papel é atribuído sem evidência. Um token que varia e não traz marcador reconhecível é informado como não posicionado, com os seus valores, para que o chamador possa perguntar ao usuário. Uma árvore parcialmente impossível de analisar importa o que puder e informa o resto, em vez de retornar uma resposta plausível, mas errada; o caminho mais antigo ``consolidate`` perdia, em vez disso, imagens sem gerar erro.

Dropped labels are zeroed out of the mask *before* morphology or intensity is computed, so excluding 495 of 500 objects costs 5 objects' worth of work, not 500.
records.translation: ``context`` é um :class:`RegionContext` que traz o tipo de objeto, a máscara de rótulos, a matriz crescente dos seus identificadores de rótulo diferentes de zero e (calculados apenas se o hook os solicitar) os seus centroides. O hook retorna uma matriz booleana de ``len(context.labels)``: ``True`` mantém o objeto, ``False`` o descarta. Os rótulos descartados são zerados na máscara *antes* que a morfologia ou a intensidade sejam calculadas, de modo que excluir 495 de 500 objetos custa o trabalho de 5 objetos, e não de 500.

records.context: A hook that raises, returns ``None``, or returns the wrong shape/dtype gets its exception re-raised as :class:`MeasurementHookError` (a :class:`spacr.errors.ConfigurationError`) naming the hook and the field. It is raised inside ``_measure_crop_core``'s ``try``, so it takes the ordinary per-field failure route: the traceback is printed, the field is recorded on the ``RunLedger`` as a failure, and ``measurements.db`` is stamped incomplete. records.source: A cell with four pathogens in it has four rows in ``pathogen`` and one in ``cell``. Putting a pathogen measurement on the same axis as a cell measurement means rolling those four up into one number -- and which number depends entirely on what is being measured:
records.translation: Uma célula com quatro patógenos dentro tem quatro linhas em ``pathogen`` e uma em ``cell``. Colocar uma medição de patógeno no mesmo eixo que uma medição de célula significa reduzir essas quatro a um único número -- e qual número depende inteiramente do que está sendo medido:

records.context: area, perimeter, integrated intensity, counts   -> SUM minimum intensity                               -> MIN of the four maximum intensity                               -> MAX of the four mean, median                                    -> the object mean/median shape descriptors, positions                    -> mean text                                            -> the first

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.translation: área, perímetro, intensidade integrada, contagens   -> SUM intensidade mínima                               -> MIN das quatro intensidade máxima                               -> MAX das quatro média, mediana                                    -> a média/mediana do objeto descritores de forma, posições                    -> média texto                                            -> o primeiro

records.context: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse structured-data name and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse key and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.translation: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` já faz essa junção e agrega cada coluna numérica com ``mean``. Isso responde silenciosamente a uma pergunta diferente para cada coluna: a área total de quatro patógenos se torna uma área média, uma contagem se torna uma contagem média e um mínimo se torna uma média de mínimos, que não é o mínimo de coisa alguma. Fora isso, a junção é correta -- é nela que ficam o vínculo com o pai, a chave de série temporal e as verificações de cardinalidade --, por isso este módulo altera o que a agregação é, e não como as tabelas se encontram.

records.context: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.label: spacr.pipeline_graph#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.translation: **Desatualizado não é ausente.** Um artefato cujas entradas mudaram está desatualizado — o número nele já não decorre dos arquivos que nomeia. Um artefato que foi excluído está ausente — um problema de disponibilidade. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` já se recusa a confundi-los, e este módulo também: um nó pode ser ambos, e :attr:`Node.state` informa ausente primeiro, porque um arquivo que não está lá não pode ser relido para verificar qualquer outra coisa.

records.context: **The registry is not the only source of truth.** A project can have run nothing at all, and a graph of zero nodes tells that user nothing. So :func:`module_graph` draws the *static* DAG from :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — what feeds what, by declaration — and :func:`build_graph` records which modules of it have actually produced something. The application view shows the module DAG behind the artifact DAG for exactly that reason: an empty project still gets a picture of the workflow it is about to execute.

records.translation: **O registro não é a única fonte de verdade.** Um projeto pode não ter executado nada, e um grafo de zero nós não diz nada a esse usuário. records.context: A merge that silently changed how a measurement was combined produces a number that is wrong and looks fine, so :class:`PlateMerge` carries what the panel has to say: the anchor and the row count, the rows each source contributed, the measurements ``columns='common'`` dropped, the laboratory microplate ids shared across screens -- and every column that fell through to :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` because no rule matched it. That last set is recomputed by re-walking ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`) rather than listed anywhere, so it cannot drift out of step with the rules.
records.label: spacr.plate_measurements#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A merge that silently changed how a measurement was combined produces a number that is wrong and looks fine, so :class:`PlateMerge` carries what the panel has to say: the anchor and the row count, the rows each source contributed, the measurements ``columns='common'`` dropped, the plate ids shared across screens -- and every column that fell through to :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` because no rule matched it. That last set is recomputed by re-walking ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`) rather than listed anywhere, so it cannot drift out of step with the rules.
records.translation: Uma mesclagem que alterasse silenciosamente a forma como uma medição foi combinada produziria um número errado com boa aparência, por isso :class:`PlateMerge` traz o que o painel precisa dizer: a âncora e o número de linhas, as linhas com que cada fonte contribuiu, as medições que ``columns='common'`` descartou, os identificadores de placa compartilhados entre triagens -- e cada coluna que recaiu em :data:`spacr.merge_tables.DEFAULT_AGGREGATION` porque nenhuma regra correspondeu a ela. Esse último conjunto é recalculado percorrendo novamente ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`), e não listado em lugar algum, de modo que não pode sair de sincronia com as regras.

This module composes existing functions instead:

records.source: This module adds no merge logic of its own. spaCR already has four places that join measurement tables, and one of them (``io._read_and_join_tables``) aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``, which turns four pathogens' total area into an average area and a minimum into a mean of minima. This module composes existing functions instead:
records.translation: Este módulo não acrescenta lógica de mesclagem própria. O spaCR já tem quatro lugares que unem tabelas de medições, e um deles (``io._read_and_join_tables``) agrega cada coluna numérica com ``mean``, o que transforma a área total de quatro patógenos em uma área média e um mínimo em uma média de mínimos. Em vez disso, este módulo compõe funções existentes:

records.context: ``read_merged`` is *many databases, one table*. ``merge_tables`` is *one database, many tables* -- and it takes a PATH, so it cannot be handed a frame that has already been stacked across databases. This feature needs both, so the composition is: read each chosen table across every database, then roll the children onto the anchor.
records.label: spacr.plate_measurements#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``read_merged`` is *many databases, one table*. ``merge_tables`` is *one database, many tables* -- and it takes a PATH, so it cannot be handed a frame that has already been stacked across databases. This feature needs both, so the composition is: read each chosen table across every database, then roll the children onto the anchor.
records.translation: ``read_merged`` é *muitos bancos de dados, uma tabela*. ``merge_tables`` é *um banco de dados, muitas tabelas* -- e recebe um PATH (caminho), de modo que não pode receber uma tabela que já foi empilhada entre bancos de dados. Este recurso precisa de ambos, então a composição é: ler cada tabela escolhida em todos os bancos de dados e, depois, reduzir os filhos sobre a âncora.

records.context: The module handles three issues:
records.label: spacr.profiler#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module handles three issues:
records.translation: O módulo trata de três questões:

records.context: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a class label, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.label: spacr.profiler#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a CLASS LABEL, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.translation: **Os backends de regressão preveem de formas diferentes.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` abrange resultados do statsmodels (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, quatro famílias GLM, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), estimadores do scikit-learn (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) e o ajustador horseshoe. :func:`predict` é a única chamada que funciona com todos eles, e :func:`response_scale` nomeia o que foi retornado — porque um GLM-binomial retorna uma probabilidade, um GLM de Poisson retorna uma taxa, e ``LinearSVC.predict`` retorna um RÓTULO DE CLASSE, o que desenharia uma função degrau e pareceria um achado. O backend hinge é perfilado por meio de ``decision_function`` exatamente por esse motivo, e a escala o indica.

records.context: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.label: spacr.profiler#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.translation: **Nada aqui é reajustado.** O modelo fornecido é o modelo perfilado. Um perfilador que reajusta silenciosamente está mostrando ao usuário um segundo modelo e rotulando-o como o primeiro, e, em um backend penalizado com ``alpha='auto'``, o segundo nem sequer é o mesmo modelo. Quando o chamador tem apenas os coeficientes gravados e nenhum objeto ativo, :func:`from_coefficients` constrói um :class:`FittedLinear` em torno deles — isso é *ler* o ajuste, e não repeti-lo, e a classe informa qual função de ligação está aplicando.

records.context: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.label: spacr.profiler#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.translation: **Um valor mantido é uma escolha, não um padrão.** :func:`reference_row` escolhe a mediana de cada coluna e declara explicitamente que o fez; o argumento ``at`` substitui qualquer um deles; e cada :class:`Profile` traz o vetor completo de valores mantidos, de modo que uma curva sempre pode ser rastreada até as suposições que a produziram.

records.context: The order the branches are tried in is load-bearing:
records.label: spacr.profiler.predict#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The order the branches are tried in is load-bearing:
records.translation: A ordem em que os ramos são tentados é essencial:

records.context: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (the ``hinge`` backend) has both that and ``predict``, and its ``predict`` returns a 0/1 CLASS. A profile of a class label is a step function, which reads as a finding and is an artefact of asking the wrong method. 2. a statsmodels results object — ``predict(exog)`` applies the inverse link, so a GLM comes back on the response scale. ``offset`` is passed when the object accepts one. 3. anything else with ``predict`` — the scikit-learn regressors. 4. the linear predictor from ``params`` / ``coef_``, for a fitted object that carries coefficients and nothing else (the horseshoe fitter).
records.label: spacr.profiler.predict#2

records.translation: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (o backend ``hinge``) tem tanto esse método quanto ``predict``, e o seu ``predict`` retorna uma CLASSE 0/1. Um perfil de um rótulo de classe é uma função degrau, que parece um achado e é um artefato de se chamar o método errado. 2. um objeto de resultados do statsmodels — ``predict(exog)`` aplica a função de ligação inversa, de modo que um GLM é retornado na escala da resposta. ``offset`` é passado quando o objeto o aceita. 3. qualquer outra coisa com ``predict`` — os regressores do scikit-learn. 4. o preditor linear a partir de ``params`` / ``coef_``, para um objeto ajustado que traz coeficientes e nada mais (o ajustador horseshoe).
